Colorectal cancer :: Signs and symptoms :: chunk_0001
The signs and symptoms of colorectal cancer depend on the location of the [tumor](/wiki/Tumor "Tumor") in the [bowel](/wiki/Bowel "Bowel"), and whether it has spread elsewhere in the body ([metastasis](/wiki/Metastasis "Metastasis")). The classic warning signs include worsening [constipation](/wiki/Constipation "Constipation"), blood in the [stool](/wiki/Stool_test "Stool test"), a decrease in stool caliber (thickness), loss of appetite, loss of weight, and [nausea](/wiki/Nausea "Nausea") or [vomiting](/wiki/Vomiting "Vomiting") in someone over 50 years old.[[12]](#cite_note-12) Around 50% of people who have colorectal cancer do not report any symptoms.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

[Rectal bleeding](/wiki/Rectal_bleeding "Rectal bleeding") or [anemia](/wiki/Anemia "Anemia") are high-risk symptoms in people over the age of 50.[[14]](#cite_note-Sym11-14) Weight loss and changes in a person's bowel habit are typically only concerning if they are associated with rectal bleeding.[[14]](#cite_note-Sym11-14)[[15]](#cite_note-pmid21624112-15)

Gastroenterologist Dr. Trisha Pasricha advises that understanding personal "normal" bowel habits and watching for unchanging, sausage-like stool consistency is crucial for early detection.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

75–95% of colorectal cancer cases occur in people with little or no genetic risk.[[17]](#cite_note-Cause11-17)[[18]](#cite_note-Lancet10-18) Risk factors include older age, male sex,[[18]](#cite_note-Lancet10-18) high intake of fat, [sugar](/wiki/Sugar "Sugar"), [alcohol](/wiki/Alcohol_(drug) "Alcohol (drug)"), [red meat](/wiki/Red_meat "Red meat"), [processed meats](/wiki/Processed_meat "Processed meat"), [obesity](/wiki/Obesity "Obesity"), [smoking](/wiki/Smoking "Smoking"), and a lack of [physical exercise](/wiki/Physical_exercise "Physical exercise").[[17]](#cite_note-Cause11-17)[[19]](#cite_note-WCRF2011-19) Approximately 10% of cases are linked to insufficient physical activity.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

President Kennedy meets in the [Oval Office](/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office") with General [Curtis LeMay](/wiki/Curtis_LeMay "Curtis LeMay") and the reconnaissance pilots who found the missile sites in Cuba.

The US had no plan for a response in place because it had never expected that the Soviets would install nuclear missiles on Cuba. [EXCOMM](/wiki/EXCOMM "EXCOMM") discussed several possible courses of action:[[82]](#cite_note-82)

1. Do nothing: American vulnerability to Soviet missiles was not new.
2. Diplomacy: Use diplomatic pressure to induce the Soviet Union to remove the missiles.
3. Secret approach: Offer Castro the choice of parting from the Soviets or being invaded.
4. Invasion: Full-force invasion of Cuba and overthrow of Castro.
5. Air strike: Use the US Air Force to attack all known missile sites.
6. Blockade: Use the US Navy to block any missiles from arriving in Cuba.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Cuban_Missile_Crisis_Game_Tree.svg/500px-Cuban_Missile_Crisis_Game_Tree.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Cuban_Missile_Crisis_Game_Tree.svg)

Houston has continued to grow into the 21st century, with the population increasing 15.7% from 2000 to 2022.[[48]](#cite_note-48)

Oil and gas have continued to fuel Houston's economic growth, with major oil companies including [Phillips 66](/wiki/Phillips_66 "Phillips 66"), [ConocoPhillips](/wiki/ConocoPhillips "ConocoPhillips"), [Occidental Petroleum](/wiki/Occidental_Petroleum "Occidental Petroleum"), [Halliburton](/wiki/Halliburton "Halliburton"), and [ExxonMobil](/wiki/ExxonMobil "ExxonMobil") having their headquarters in the Houston area. In 2001, [Enron Corporation](/wiki/Enron_Corporation "Enron Corporation"), a Houston company with $100 billion in revenue, became engulfed in an [accounting scandal](/wiki/Enron_scandal "Enron scandal") which bankrupted the company in 2001.[[49]](#cite_note-49) Healthcare had also emerged as a major industry in Houston. The [Texas Medical Center](/wiki/Texas_Medical_Center "Texas Medical Center") is now the largest medical complex in the world and employs over 120,000 people.[[50]](#cite_note-50)

In the first decade of the 21st century, three new sports stadiums opened downtown. In 2000, the [Houston Astros](/wiki/Houston_Astros "Houston Astros") opened their new baseball stadium, [Daikin Park](/wiki/Daikin_Park "Daikin Park"), in downtown adjacent to the old [Union Station](/wiki/Union_Station_(Houston) "Union Station (Houston)"). The [Houston Texans](/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") were formed in 2002 as an [NFL](/wiki/NFL "NFL") expansion team, replacing the [Houston Oilers](/wiki/Houston_Oilers "Houston Oilers"), which had left the city in 1996. [NRG Stadium](/wiki/NRG_Stadium "NRG Stadium") opened the same year. In 2003, the [Toyota Center](/wiki/Toyota_Center "Toyota Center") opened as the home for the [Houston Rockets](/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets"). In 2005, the [Houston Dynamo](/wiki/Houston_Dynamo "Houston Dynamo") soccer team was formed. The West Coast of the United States has an [oceanic climate](/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") in its Northwestern, Northern, and Eastern edge towards the U.S.-Canada border, but from Northern California, towards the U.S.-Mexico border the climate is [Mediterranean](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate"). While the northern half of the west coast, particularly coastal Washington and Oregon has moderate rainfall, particularly during the winter months, much of coastal California is drier year-round.

The coastline sees significantly milder temperatures compared to inland areas during summer. In far Northern California there is a difference of 17 °C (30 °F) between [Eureka](/wiki/Eureka,_California "Eureka, California") and [Willow Creek](/wiki/Willow_Creek,_California "Willow Creek, California") despite only 25 miles (40 km) separating the locations and Willow Creek being located at a 500 metres (1,600 ft) elevation. Slightly narrower fluctuations can be seen all through the coastline, and could partially be explained by the cold currents in the Pacific Ocean moderating coastal temperatures and the mountain ranges blocking the maritime air from moving farther inland than its foothills during summer.[[12]](#cite_note-blue_planet-13)

Daejeon citizens are recognized for their fondness of nature, with most mountains, hot springs, and rivers freely open for public use. Many of the city's modern-day traditions, festivals, attractions, and industries are linked in some way to important mountains, rivers, and forests.[[7]](#cite_note-HT-7)

The soundtrack to *The Abyss* was composed by [Alan Silvestri](/wiki/Alan_Silvestri "Alan Silvestri") and released by [Varèse Sarabande](/wiki/Var%C3%A8se_Sarabande "Varèse Sarabande") on August 22, 1989.[[48]](#cite_note-OriginalScore-50) In 2014, they issued a limited-edition (3,000 copies), two-disc album featuring the complete score minus the end credits medley, which is absent from both releases, and has a 113 minute-running time. Considered to be one of Silvestri's most accomplished 1980s works, the music score is a mixture of [orchestral](/wiki/Orchestral "Orchestral") and [electronic music](/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music") which combines dark, ethereal [ambient](/wiki/Ambient_music "Ambient music") sounds with a wave of intense, [militaristic action sequences](/wiki/Martial_music "Martial music"), before it climaxes with some of the most orchestral, sweeping [choral](/wiki/Choral "Choral") music. The score features light [harps](/wiki/Harp "Harp"), [chimes](/wiki/Chime_(bell_instrument) "Chime (bell instrument)"), [string](/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument") sustains, electronic textures, continuous drums, pulsating [brass](/wiki/Brass_instrument "Brass instrument") [clusters](/wiki/Tone_cluster "Tone cluster"), [percussive](/wiki/Percussive "Percussive") rumbling and rhythmic interjections from [xylophones](/wiki/Xylophone "Xylophone").[[49]](#cite_note-UK-51)

The score "opens with a preview of the romantic and redeeming themes that Silvestri would largely save until the climax of the film",[[50]](#cite_note-track-52) and features "a couple of recurring [melodic ideas](/wiki/Theme_music "Theme music") that weave their way through the music".[[49]](#cite_note-UK-51) However, unlike other Silvestri's works, "there is no thematic material weaved into the action".
